_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); discount-retail signals

pit_profile.why: Walmart: 'helps people around the world save money and live better – anytime and anywhere – by providing the opportunity to shop in retail stores and through eCommerce'; 'everyday low prices ("EDLP")'; 'We operate in the highly competitive omni-channel retail industry in all of the markets we serve' ('We face strong competition from other retailers and wholesale club operators which could materially adversely affect our financial performance'); and 'General economic conditions and other economic factors, globally or in one or more of the markets we serve, may adversely affect our financial performance' (its own FY2021 10-K): a low-price store network whose demand follows the consumer economy by its own account; ECOMMERCE is live (from 2015-01-01) and its competition risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Walmart

theme_watch.reason: Live: Walmart's own FY2021 10-K says 'Each of our segments competes for customers, employees, digital prominence, products and services and in other important aspects of its business with many other local, regional, national and global physical, eCommerce and omni-channel retailers, wholesale club operators and retail intermediaries.' At the same time it sells online itself: 'Walmart U.S. eCommerce sales positively contributed approximately 5.4% and 2.1% to comparable sales for fiscal 2021 and 2020, respectively'. The stock trades at 25.7x FY22E — a premium. The theme registry dates the market's pricing of e-commerce to 2017-06-16 (Amazon agrees to buy Whole Foods; grocers and food retailers sell off the same day), evidence that names no company. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ECOMMERCE) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing online substitution of Walmart's store sales specifically.

classification.quality_note: Walmart: 'helps people around the world save money and live better – anytime and anywhere – by providing the opportunity to shop in retail stores and through eCommerce'; 'everyday low prices ("EDLP")'; 'We operate in the highly competitive omni-channel retail industry in all of the markets we serve' ('We face strong competition from other retailers and wholesale club operators which could materially adversely affect our financial performance'); and 'General economic conditions and other economic factors, globally or in one or more of the markets we serve, may adversely affect our financial performance' (its own FY2021 10-K): a low-price store network whose demand follows the consumer economy by its own account; ECOMMERCE is live (from 2015-01-01) and its competition risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Walmart. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; +83% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.70; conservative 2yr -24%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -9.5%/yr (worst year FY12-FY21, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +9.8%/yr (Q4 ex-FX + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +9.8%/yr (FY12-FY21 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +9.8%/yr (best 2-yr run FY12-FY21); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: WMT (retrospective, 2021-04-16) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B infx (59.5% downside to Bear $57 / +-6.1% upside to Bull $132) | Adj composite 2.05 vs market 3.75: gap -1.70 [OVERVALUED] | +83% above the EPP floor $77 (14x FY22E $5.48) | Conservative 2-yr case: -24.3% total (-12.1%/yr) | At 25.7x FY22E the 15% hurdle price $186 sits above the BULL case; U.S. comps +8.5% in Q4 FY21, forward sales +7.6% (no FY22 net sales guide in numbers, Q4 FY21 net sales at constant currency); e-commerce competition is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
